date.noteEn: The Met gives an approximate span and dates Shuppiluliuma I's reign to 1370–1330 BCE.

events.titleEn: The Hittite empire reaches its greatest extent
events.summaryEn: After years of campaigning, the Hittite empire, ruled from Hattusha (Boğazköy), reaches its greatest extent in central and southeastern Anatolia and in lands to the south bordering Egyptian territory. Its ruler Shuppiluliuma I is both a general and a builder of large stone structures with reliefs.
events.geographyEn: Central and southeastern Anatolia and lands to the south
events.selectionNote: Records the Hittite empire at its greatest extent.

events.titleEn: The Mycenaean palace at Pylos thrives
events.summaryEn: The Mycenaean palace at Pylos, the best preserved of its kind, thrives. Its clay Linear B tablets suggest a king at the head of a highly organised feudal system.
events.selectionNote: The catalog dates the burning of the Pylos palace to 1200 BCE. This record covers its earlier prosperity.

events.titleEn: San José Mogote raises the first public building in the Valley of Oaxaca
events.summaryEn: Builders at San José Mogote, the major regional centre of the Valley of Oaxaca, construct the valley's first public building. It is a stuccoed wattle-and-daub structure on a platform-like foundation.
events.geographyEn: San José Mogote, Valley of Oaxaca, Mexico
events.selectionNote: Marks the start of public architecture in the Valley of Oaxaca.

date.noteEn: The Met gives an approximate span for the building.

events.titleEn: Untash-Napirisha builds the ziggurat complex at Chogha Zanbil
events.summaryEn: King Untash-Napirisha builds a new capital and religious complex with a ziggurat at Chogha Zanbil. Glazed blue and green terracotta covers the ziggurat's facade, and glass and ivory mosaics decorate its interior.
events.selectionNote: A royal Elamite capital and temple complex; no catalog record covers it.
